thesis: JPMorgan Chase is a universal bank with consumer, corporate and markets franchises with ROE of 17.4% TTM on reported equity. Against the configured valuation grid the base fair value is 252.56 versus a 318.90 close (-20.8%), so the stock already prices in more than the filings support.

strengths.point: Durable deposit franchise scale and diversified fee businesses.
P/E of 13.0x on TTM earnings with ROE of 17.4% TTM on reported equity.

risks.point: Key risk: credit normalisation and lower net interest income as policy rates fall.
Base fair value sits 20.8% below the last close.

invalidation_rationale: The fundamental kill condition is a business metric, not a price: a sustained decline in TTM operating income or a cut to capital returns would break the thesis.
conviction_reason: The price sits above most of the valuation grid.
self_evidence_reason: TTM, FY history and the valuation grid were available from SEC companyfacts.
missing_data: From fundamentals data: ttm.capex: missing in SEC companyfacts - FCF, FCF margin and FCF yield not computed
Reverse DCF implied growth (not computable for this sector class)

sources.title: Valuation grid for JPM derived from SEC companyfacts

valuation.method: Configured P/E and P/B bands (financials: DCF cells have limited meaning) plus one FCF DCF cell.

extensions.quality_notes: JPMorgan Chase: ROE of 17.4% TTM on reported equity; moat rests on its deposit franchise scale and diversified fee businesses.
extensions.balance_sheet_notes: Balance-sheet leverage is assessed through capital ratios that SEC companyfacts does not expose; equity and earnings figures are taken as reported.
